rows.act: A farm grinds up live male chicks because they can't lay eggs.
A supplier boils silkworms alive in their cocoons to harvest silk.
Force-feeding ducks through a pipe to enlarge their livers for foie gras.
Trapping foxes in steel leg-hold traps for their fur.
A mine uses child labor because children are cheaper and fit narrow shafts.
A company dumps untreated chemical waste into a river to save money.
A lab breeds dogs with deformed skulls that can barely breathe because buyers like the look.
Plucking fur from live angora rabbits.
Whipping racehorses to make them run faster.
A hatchery culls lower-yield hens early to keep the flock's output efficient.
A farm debeaks hens as a standard practice to reduce pecking losses.
A fishery keeps stocking density high because lower density cuts into margins.
A grocery sources only cage-produced eggs because they are cheaper for customers.
A company runs unpaid 'trial shifts' as part of its standard hiring process.
A zoo keeps a solitary elephant because a second one isn't in the budget.
A logistics firm sets delivery quotas that make bathroom breaks impractical.
A farm transports livestock for 20 hours without water to reach a cheaper processor.
A farm uses gestation crates because group housing needs more land.
A retailer keeps prices low by sourcing wool from mulesed sheep.
A company recruits from low-wage regions to avoid local labor protections.
A dairy farm separates newborn calves from their mothers within hours of birth to harvest their milk.
A pork producer confines pregnant sows in narrow metal crates where they cannot turn around.
A poultry operation trims chicks' beaks without anesthesia to prevent feather pecking.
A cattle ranch castrates baby bulls with a hot iron without pain relief.
A shrimp farm drains antibiotic-laden water directly onto adjacent farmland after each harvest.
A sheep farm docks lambs' tails without anesthesia to meet meat market standards.
A fish farm uses nets that shred fish skin during routine antibiotic treatments.
A goat dairy culls male kids at birth because they have no commercial value.
A turkey farm keeps birds in windowless barns with ammonia levels that burn their eyes.
A honey producer burns bee colonies with smoke and replaces their honey with sugar syrup.
A veal facility chains calves to wooden stalls that prevent them from lying down.
A fish plant dumps millions of heads and guts into landfills instead of recycling them.
A cosmetics company drips toxic chemicals into rabbits' eyes to test for irritation.
A pharmaceutical lab injects mice with high doses of experimental drugs until their organs fail.
A testing facility forces dogs to inhale concentrated cleaning product fumes to measure lung damage.
A university lab breeds pigs with genetic defects that cause chronic spinal pain.
A research center performs surgery on conscious primates without anesthesia to map nerve responses.
A drug tester forces rats to drink pesticide-laced water to observe poisoning symptoms.
A veterinary supplier breeds cats with inherited kidney disease to sell to research labs.
A testing firm injects new paint ingredients under guinea pigs' skin to measure allergies.
A laboratory keeps dolphins in concrete tanks while researchers attach sensors to study stress.
A cosmetic firm shaves rabbits' backs and applies chemical irritants to measure skin corrosion.
A medical device company implants faulty wires into rats' brains to test nerve stimulation.
A research lab forces chickens to stand on electrified grids to study chronic foot pain.
A garment factory locks its doors during shifts to prevent workers from leaving.
A construction company withholds passports from migrant workers to prevent them from quitting.
A warehouse company tracks bathroom breaks with scanners and docks pay for every second over the limit.
A fishing company forces crew members to work eighteen-hour days without proper safety gear.
A domestic agency charges workers recruitment fees that leave them in immediate debt.
A factory owner forces pregnant employees to stand on concrete floors for twelve hours.
A logistics company fires workers who organize to discuss wages and replaces them with undocumented laborers.
A mining corporation forces adults to work in underground tunnels with no ventilation.
A restaurant chain requires employees to pay for their own uniforms and refuses to refund them upon termination.
A plantation owner forces workers to live in company housing where they are charged for utilities and food.
A tech company outsources data labeling to workers who earn less than a dollar per hour.
A chemical plant discharges untreated cyanide directly into a nearby creek to avoid wastewater treatment fees.
A logging company clear-cuts ancient rainforests to plant monoculture palm oil trees.
A mining corporation blows up mountaintops to access coal and dumps the rock into adjacent valleys.
A plastic manufacturer discharges microbeads into municipal water systems without filtration.
A shipping company dumps ballast water containing invasive species into a protected coastal bay.
A farm applies banned pesticides that kill all pollinating insects in a three-mile radius.
A textile mill dumps arsenic-laced dye runoff into a river used by downstream communities for drinking water.
A developer pumps groundwater faster than the aquifer can recharge, causing the water table to collapse.
A coal plant releases radioactive ash into nearby lakes instead of storing it securely.
A paper mill harvests old-growth trees to make pulp, destroying critical owl nesting habitats.
A cruise company incinerates plastic waste at sea, releasing toxic dioxins into the marine atmosphere.
A supplement company sells capsules containing only rice flour while labeling them as expensive herbs.
A real estate agent knowingly sells a house built on unstable landfill without disclosing the risk.
A food manufacturer labels farm-raised trout as wild-caught salmon to charge a higher price.
A car dealer rolls back odometers on used vehicles to hide that the engines have been driven over two hundred thousand miles.
A pharmaceutical company hides clinical trial data showing that a heart medication causes fatal arrhythmias.
A jewelry store sells chemically treated glass beads as genuine diamonds.
A tech startup sells user data to advertisers while claiming it never shares personal information.
A financial advisor sells high-fee speculative bonds to elderly clients by falsely guaranteeing principal protection.
A clothing brand labels garments as 100% organic cotton when they contain mostly synthetic polyester.
A medical device company falsifies approval documents to sell a pacemaker with a known battery failure rate.
A restaurant chain mixes low-grade cooking oil with recycled motor oil to cut frying costs.
A charity organization diverts eighty percent of donated funds to executive bonuses instead of aid programs.
